title: US CPI preview: Wall Street sees cooler inflation but the Fed may not blink
body: Perhaps one of the more intriguing prospects heading into the US CPI report today is what if inflation cools and the Fed simply decides to shrug it off? Well, that may very well happen. Wall Street is expecting a softer inflation reading for October but I wouldn't be so quick to assume that it will be enough to change the Fed's thinking ahead of the December meeting. The consensus estimate is for headline inflation to rise by 0.3% m/m in October, down from 0.6% in September. Meanwhile, core inflation is expected to ease to 0.2% m/m - down from 0.3% in the month before. Morgan Stanley and Bank of America are both leaning towards an even softer headline reading of 0.2%. The former sees core inflation slowing to just 0.19%, with shelter, hotel prices, airfares and education costs normalising after September's unusually strong readings. But even so, the latter isn't quite buying the idea that cooler inflation will be enough to derail another Fed rate hike in December. BofA argues that a 0.2% core reading would still effectively lock in a December move, with "only an indisputably soft 0.1% reading could affect the calculus". title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6655 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

title: PrimeXBT Insights: NVIDIA Earnings Preview & Key Price Drivers
body: What has been reported As reported by the New York Times on 29th October, US authorities suspect a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company, of working for China's Ministry of State Security, and Huang may have been the target of a Chinese espionage effort. According to the Times, Megaspeed bought about $4.8 billion of NVIDIA hardware over two years. According to CBS News, NVIDIA's board announced on Sunday 8th November that a committee of independent directors, working with outside counsel, will investigate, and Huang has said he will cooperate fully. The investigation is ongoing and no findings have been published. China has rejected them as groundless, according to CBS News, and NVIDIA's board has said it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. Huang remains chief executive. The board has said it has confidence in him. Shareholders filed a proposed class action on Monday 9th November, according to Reuters. The complaint, filed in federal court in San Jose, California, according to The Week, alleges that NVIDIA and Huang failed to disclose his reported ties to the former Megaspeed executive. These are allegations that have not been tested in court. President Donald Trump has said the FBI is looking into the matter, according to Reuters. No FBI statement has been reported. Why it matters for the shares The risk investors are weighing is less NVIDIA's revenue than governance and policy.

title: Stock earnings pick of the week: Can Applied Materials spot cracks in the AI spending boom?
body: Spend, spend, spend. That's been the name of the game in the AI boom over the past two years. But really, just how much longer can the industry keep throwing money at bigger and better chips before someone starts asking whether the returns are worth it? Well, Applied Materials might give us a few clues this week. The semiconductor equipment giant reports earnings on Thursday this week. And just like the rest of the other tech earnings these days, I would be less interested in whether it can beat Wall Street's estimates. Instead, I'd focus much more on what the company has to say about the next round of spending. I mean you would think that if the AI investment frenzy is beginning to lose steam, then the companies supplying the tools to build those chips might be among the first to notice. Everyone loves a gold rush, especially the folks selling the shovels. And in the AI boom, Applied Materials is very much in the business of selling those shovels. Wall Street is expecting revenue of $10.30 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $4.06, compared with $6.80 billion and $2.17 respectively a year ago. That's quite a big leap and one that speaks to the relentless spending on advanced chips and manufacturing capacity. For some context, Applied Materials delivered record revenue of $9.12 billion in the previous quarter with non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.50.

In fact, although we can have a range of estimates, most forecasts might be clustered on the upper bound of the range, so even if the data comes out inside the range of estimates but on the lower bound of the range, it can still create a surprise effect. title: Macro pulse: Wall Street's relief rally is looking good but what happens next?
body: Wall Street is certainly enjoying itself again to start the new week. The S&P 500 surged by 2.3% yesterday, its best performance since April, as falling oil prices and hopes of a de-escalation in the US-Iran war gave investors a reason to pile back into stocks. Fair enough. Cheaper oil prices help to take some pressure off inflation, which then eases the squeeze on corporate costs and household spending. So, that's good news for stocks especially after the brutal selloff last week. But now, what happens when all that optimism is starting to get priced into markets? Let's think about if for a second. A potential end to the Middle East conflict removes one major source of uncertainty for equities. However, it doesn't necessarily give stocks a fresh catalyst to keep pushing higher endlessly. As such, I would argue that there are three things worth watching to judge whether this latest rebound has any staying power. The first one is that Treasury yields need to also play along. 10-year Treasury yields are hovering just below 4.90% and that's hardly an invitation for investors to throw caution to the wind. If oil prices keep falling but bond yields remain elevated, any real benefit to equity valuations could prove to be limited once the dust settles. Adding to that, Washington's fiscal outlook isn't helping either. Persistent deficits and heavy borrowing requirements could continue to underping long-term yields especially, even as geopolitical risks fade.

title: Learn technical analysis without being a professor: This repeating pattern is super simple and super effective
body: Gold futures: A breakout, a retest, and another move higher You don't need to be a professor to learn technical analysis. This simple pattern on gold's 4-hour chart offers a valuable lesson about identifying the stronger side of the market, even if you use a completely different trading strategy. My 4-hour gold chart from today, November 10, is super simple. No indicators, zero noise. And I can tell you that once you practice recognizing these patterns, they can become an extremely useful part of your trading analysis. But let's clarify something first. "Effective" does NOT mean you will always profit. Patterns matter because they give you guidance about which side of the market is currently stronger. That can help you develop an edge, although no particular win rate is guaranteed. Experience, confirmation, execution and risk management all matter. It also doesn't mean prices cannot change direction later, that other patterns don't matter, or that something unexpected won't happen five minutes from now and change the market entirely. With that in mind, let's look at gold. Gold's 4-hour chart: Three simple observations Gold futures had been moving lower inside a channel, between two downward-sloping lines. Some traders would look at this as a potential bullish continuation pattern, similar to a bull flag. Now look at the three numbered points on the chart. Point 1: The breakout Gold moved above the upper line of the descending channel. This is called a breakout.
